Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Sarah Smith, DOB: 20/04/1980 vs 20/04/1983 (conflict noted), Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Dr. Gohil, Practice: Babylon, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Anxiety symptoms associated with acute shortness of breath in the postpartum period (situational/health-related anxiety; rule out panic-related symptoms per DDx)
- Secondary: Postpartum adjustment stressors (newborn care while recovering from C-section)
- Tertiary: Not recorded
(DDx supports consideration of anxiety/panic-related dyspnea; primary medical concern is possible pulmonary embolism, but this plan addresses mental health aspects only.)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); last taken about 1 week ago
- Allergies/ADRs: Ibuprofen (reaction not described)
- Past Medical History: Cesarean section 4 weeks prior; denies other medical problems

- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Not recorded
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing: Postpartum period (4 weeks after C-section)
- Precipitating: Sudden onset shortness of breath with palpitations while at rest; health alarm
- Perpetuating: Pain/tenderness post-surgery; uncertainty about cause of symptoms; alone with newborn when symptoms began
- Protective: Help-seeking, cooperative, accepts urgent medical plan; partner present in life; awareness of family history of clots

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce acute stress/anxiety; feel calmer while addressing medical causes; maintain ability to care for newborn
- Clinical Goal(s): Ensure urgent medical evaluation and stabilization; provide brief anxiety management strategies; screen for postpartum mood/anxiety disorders at follow-up if symptoms persist after medical clearance
- Actions (Patient): 
  - Attend hospital promptly as advised
  - Avoid codeine for now (per physician advice)
  - Contact partner/family for support with baby and transport as needed
  - Use simple calming strategies (e.g., slow diaphragmatic breathing) if anxiety escalates while seeking care
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Coordinate/confirm urgent medical evaluation outcome and communicate results to patient
  - Arrange follow-up within 1–2 weeks to reassess anxiety/postpartum mental health
  - Consider brief screening (e.g., for postpartum anxiety) if medical causes are excluded and symptoms persist
  - Provide information/referral options for perinatal mental health supports if indicated

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s): Adjust to postpartum changes with adequate support
- Clinical Goal(s): Enhance practical and emotional supports; monitor for emerging postpartum mood/anxiety symptoms
- Actions (Patient): Identify and request specific support from partner/family (rest, childcare tasks); plan short rest periods
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide resources on postpartum supports; reassess stress/load at follow-up; consider referral to community/perinatal services if needed

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Postpartum clot risk, rationale for urgent hospital assessment, hold codeine temporarily
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (agreed to urgent hospital evaluation)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea and palpitations — Likelihood: Low-Medium — Justification: Reports acute stress and racing heart; anxiety can contribute to dyspnea, though medical etiologies (e.g., PE) are of higher concern and must be excluded first.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Comprehensive mental health history, risk assessment (suicide/self-harm), sleep/appetite, standardized screening scores, full social history, formal MSE, documented follow-up date
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: DOB reported as 20/04/1980 by patient; clinician stated 1983 (conflict noted). DDx focuses on medical causes; only limited support for anxiety/panic as a contributor
- Transcript quality notes: Telephone consult; limited mental health assessment; no vitals beyond pulse count; context primarily medical (acute SOB postpartum) rather than mental health-focused conversation
